bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to taxation; local government aid; modifying the minimum employment threshold to qualify as a peace officer in certain municipalities for purposes of police state aid apportionment; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 477C.01, subdivision 7, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 477C.01, subdivision 7, is amended to read:

Subd. 7.
Peace officer.
"Peace officer" means any person:
(1) whose primary source of income derived from wages is from direct employment by a municipality as a law enforcement officer on a full-time basis of not less than 30 hours per week;
(2) who has been employed for a minimum of:

(i) two months before December 31 preceding the date of the current year's certification under section 477C.02, subdivision 1, by a statutory or home rule charter city, town, or county with a population of less than 5,000;

(ii) six months before December 31 preceding the date of the current year's certification under section 477C.02, subdivision 1, by a statutory or home rule charter city, town, or county with a population of 5,000 or more; or

(iii) six months before December 31 preceding the date of the current year's certification under section 477C.02, subdivision 1, by a municipality that is not a statutory or home rule charter city, town, or county;
(3) who is sworn to enforce the general criminal laws of the state and local ordinances;
(4) who is licensed by the Peace Officers Standards and Training Board and is authorized to arrest with a warrant; and
(5) who is a member of the State Patrol retirement plan or the public employees police and fire fund.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective for aids payable in calendar year 2026 and thereafter.

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 477C.01, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 8.

Population.

"Population" has the meaning given in section 477A.011, subdivision 3.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective for aids payable in calendar year 2026 and thereafter.
